newsitem.title: BELARUS: Council of Europe says Belarus referendum illegal.
newsitem.headline: Council of Europe says Belarus referendum illegal.

text.p: A Council of Europe delegation officially pronounced illegitimate on Wednesday the results of a referendum in Belarus which gave President Alexander Lukashenko sweeping powers.

A committee from the pan-European body, set up after World War Two to promote human rights and democracy, said in a statement released at a news conference that it was impossible "to reach a positive conclusion as to the democratic legitimacy of the referendum and its results."

Appealing to Lukashenko to respect parliamentary democracy and the rule of law, the statement expressed concern that the way a new legislature was being formed "might deprive the Belarussian Parliament of its legitimacy".
About 110 deputies have accepted Lukashenko's invitation to set up the lower house of a new parliament, leaving a rump of some 60 deputies who oppose him sitting in the official parliament chamber.
The statement said the way the referendum was organised "was contrary to democratic standards and jeopardised the future of democratic development in Belarus".

The delegates held a two-hour meeting with Lukashenko which their chairman described as "two monologues rather than a dialogue". They told him Belarus -- the only European country outside former Yugoslavia which has not joined the Council -- would have to meet its minimum standards before it did.
